abstract: How the brain coordinates the removal of degenerating neurons with host rest and activity remains poorly understood. Using longitudinal two-photon imaging in mice with cytosolic TDP-43 proteinopathy, we show that microglia remove neuronal corpses through an ordered sequence of reaching, approaching, isolating and digesting. Clearance was higher during the light (resting) phase and lower during the dark (active) phase. This pattern reversed after light-dark cycle inversion and was blunted by sleep disruption. Chemogenetic inhibition of locus coeruleus noradrenergic neurons increased engulfment during the active phase, while activation and inhibition of the {beta}2-adrenergic receptor ADRB2 suppressed and enhanced clearance, respectively, identifying noradrenergic signaling as a brake on engulfment. However, sustained microglial ADRB2 deletion impaired clearance and blunted light-dark differences. These findings reveal that microglial removal of degenerating neurons is enhanced during rest and support a role for noradrenergic signaling in coordinating this cellular maintenance process with the host's rest-activity cycle.
